title: Go HTTP Server Patterns & Graceful Shutdown

scenes.line1: How do you stop a Go server
scenes.say: Ever wondered how to stop a Go HTTP server without losing user requests? Let's break down graceful shutdown.

scenes.label: Concurrent
scenes.sub: Go's net HTTP server handles many requests at once.
scenes.say: Go's net HTTP server handles lots of requests at the same time, thanks to built-in concurrency.
Here's how it works: start the server, listen for a shutdown signal, call Shutdown to finish in-flight requests, then exit cleanly.

scenes.code:
srv := &http.Server{Addr: ":8080"}
go srv.ListenAndServe()
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(
  context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
srv.Shutdown(ctx)
scenes.say: In practice, create your server, run it in a goroutine, then use context with timeout and call Shutdown. This gives users time to finish up.

scenes.question: Is closing the listener enough?
scenes.right: No, you must use Shutdown to let active requests finish before stopping.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: just closing the listener isn't enough. Always use Shutdown to let current requests complete.
